title: Custom-node requirements reinstall the CUDA torch stack over the CPU one
description: Found live on Linux 2026-07-30 while verifying MPI-406; this is the second and larger half of it. downloadManager.js:2181 runs pip install -r <node requirements> --upgrade through runPipCommand (shared.js:284), a bare python -m pip with NO index constraint, so torch resolves from default PyPI = the CUDA build. --upgrade is what makes it fire on an already-correct engine: the comment at downloadManager.js:2033 claims "pip with --upgrade is idempotent (a no-op when already satisfied)", which is wrong - it pulls the newest for every listed package AND its dependencies, replacing a correct CPU torch with the newest CUDA one. Measured: ComfyUI-LTXVideo/requirements.txt dragged in torch, torchvision, triton, cuda-toolkit and 14 nvidia-* wheels on a box with no NVIDIA driver. The repo already learned this mechanism once - nodesDeps.js:178, MPI-217, opencv 4.13 to 5.0 across the whole engine. Dropping the torch lines via the existing requirementsDrop machinery is NOT sufficient: timm and diffusers depend on torch/torchvision, so --upgrade bumps them transitively regardless. Candidates, in order: a constraints file pinning the torch family while keeping --upgrade self-heal; dropping --upgrade (matches the comment, pipPins is the corrective path); or a vendor-aware CPU index-url (fixes torch only, not the general drift class). runPipCommand is a SHARED primitive with callers across both engine twins - sweep them all before changing it. Severity: wasteful not broken, a CUDA torch runs on CPU, but it is several GB on the machines least able to afford it and contributed to a thermal shutdown on the box that found it.
